endorsements.title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for AI-Enabled Device Software Functions (final guidance)
endorsements.quote: To help facilitate FDA's review, it may be helpful to clearly establish boundaries or guardrails that define the range of automatic updates.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Once deployed by the implementer team, the AI solution is often handed over to a model operations team (when available) to provide ongoing monitoring, retraining, and governance of models to ensure peak performance and that decisions are transparent.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
endorsements.quote: A description of how the model will be updated and maintained over time, if applicable.

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: For models that update their parameters on new data, whether through scheduled retraining or ongoing learning, the register should capture not only the original training dataset but also the mechanism by which new data enters the model, the cadence and criteria for updates, and who is responsible for approving those updates.

endorsements.title: Diverging regulatory DNA in adaptive medical AI: US agility and EU accountability in lifecycle governance
endorsements.quote: Accordingly, governing adaptive medical AI requires more than extending legacy device paradigms: it demands explicit definitions of permissible update types, pre-specified validation and documentation expectations, and post-market monitoring triggers that determine when performance changes warrant escalation, notification, or re-assessment.

endorsements.title: Governing Patient-Facing AI-Generated Video in Digital Health: A Risk-and-Ethics Matrix for Deployment, Monitoring, and Change Control
endorsements.quote: Third, change control should be planned rather than improvised: institutions should prespecify anticipated model, prompt, or pipeline updates and the evidence required to maintain assurance over time, drawing on the Food and Drug Administration’s predetermined change control plan approach for AI-enabled systems.

evidence.title: Self-Aware SGD: Reliable Incremental Adaptation Framework for Clinical AI Models
evidence.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
evidence.outcome: Reliability of incremental model updates under label noise and distribution shift with a sanity-check filter
evidence.effect: Self-aware SGD, which filters unreliable gradient updates, is reported to give reliable incremental updates under distribution shift with label noise. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Experimental evaluations on the Oxford University Hospital datasets highlight that self-aware SGD can provide reliable incremental updates for overcoming distribution shifts in challenging conditions induced by label noise.

commentary.bottom_line: Six sources, including two FDA guidance documents, endorse defining bounds for automatic model updates, but only one offline benchmark study tests a related mechanism, and it reports no numbers. Health systems can ask developers for update plans on regulatory and governance grounds, though no study shows an effect on clinical performance or patient harm.

perspectives.view: One study tests a filter that screens unreliable gradient updates in an offline benchmark and reports that updates stayed reliable under distribution shift and label noise. The abstract gives no numbers. The design is simulated, the setting is not clinical, and the intervention is an algorithm rather than a documented update plan, so certainty is very low.

No study in this set documents harm from drift in continuously learning clinical models, and none measures whether predefined update bounds catch unsafe behavior before it reaches patients. The benchmark result suggests that an automated sanity check may block some unreliable updates, which is one way to enforce bounds, but its performance on clinical data is unknown.

FDA's final change control plan guidance says it may be helpful to set boundaries on automatic updates, and the draft lifecycle guidance says submissions should describe how a model will be updated and maintained. These positions rest on regulatory reasoning rather than trial evidence. A commentary comparing US and EU approaches calls for explicit definitions of permissible update types.

CHAI playbooks ask that model registers record how new data enters a model, the cadence and criteria for updates, and who is responsible. No study tests whether this documentation stays current in real workflows, how often it is consulted, or how much staff time it requires.

CHAI guidance hands ongoing retraining and monitoring to a model operations team when one is available, which suggests some health systems lack that staff. No study in this set estimates the cost or staffing needed to review developer update plans or to monitor models against stated bounds.

The only test used an offline benchmark with no patients, so it gives no information about Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Whether update bounds protect model performance for these groups when their data shift has not been studied.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares deployed clinical models updated within predefined bounds against models updated without them on drift, subgroup performance, or patient harm. Studies are also needed on whether developer descriptions of update and maintenance plans are complete and whether health systems use them in oversight.
commentary.underserved_note: The single test was an offline benchmark with no patient population, so no evidence addresses Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy groups. Health systems serving these populations may need to request subgroup performance checks after each update, because nothing in this evidence shows that update bounds preserve performance for them.
